title: GSOFT group-shuffle Mirror task Views
hypothesis: A shared linear weight plus short group-shuffle orthogonal View codes can reproduce independent dense task transforms with lower serialized bytes and matrix-free compute; a native GSOFT implementation should be an exact control and will determine whether the result is Mirror-specific.
physical_object: one shared FP32 D×D linear weight
mirror_coordinate: per-task packed block-orthogonal stages with deterministic group-shuffle permutations
logical_multiplicity: 16 task-specific dense logical transforms over one shared physical weight
controls: shared W plus native GSOFT group-shuffle coordinates

development.selection_metric: function output NRMSE, actual serialized bytes, MAC proxy, and CPU wall time per transform

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, matrix-free GSOFT output NRMSE <=1e-5 and at 2 stages actual payload <=50% independent while compute <=1.3x dense apply. Mirror-specific attribution additionally requires beating native GSOFT at comparable state/compute.
failure_gate: Any audit seed exceeds quality or byte/compute gates; exact native GSOFT alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution regardless of generic structured-transform feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic linear transforms generated from group-shuffle factors by construction; no trained task quality or capacity claim.
CPU wall time is local NumPy calibration only, not a fused kernel or GPU serving result.
Permutation schedule is a fixed deterministic function of shape and stage index; only the factors and schedule metadata are paid.
